fixes.explanation: I get the thinking, friend. Apostles sound official. But Paul says he was "…sent not from men nor by man…" and that rules out any group of men, even official ones. The name he gives is Jesus Christ and God the Father.

Nope, and Paul shuts that door fast. He says he was "…sent not from men nor by man…" so no human office makes the list. He names Jesus Christ and God the Father instead. Nobody in this opening line has a desk in Jerusalem.
Close to the right neighborhood, but the word isn't leaders. Paul says Jesus "…gave Himself for our sins…" It's a rescue from the present evil age.
Sounds mysterious, friend, but that's not in the text. Paul says they are "…turning to a different gospel…" Nothing secret here, just a different gospel, and I think Paul is not happy about it.

No kings in this one, baker. Paul says, "…even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be under a curse!" He names "we" and an angel from heaven, and no king shows up in that warning.
Moses is a big name, friend, but he's not in this verse. Paul says, "If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ." Christ is the One he serves.
Caesar doesn't show up anywhere in this passage, baker. Paul says, "If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ." His answer is Christ.
